Relatively safer day Relatively safer night

In detail

Sussex Police recorded 479 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 9.5 per 1,000 residents, the 8th highest rate of Brighton and Hove's 21 wards. The daytime score here is driven by shoplifting (8), vehicle crime (4), burglary (3); the evening/night score by anti social behaviour (54), violent crime (49), public order (11). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Hollingdean and Stanmer safe?

Wandroz currently rates Hollingdean and Stanmer in Brighton and Hove as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Brighton and Hove, both by day and after dark. This rating is derived from Sussex Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Hollingdean and Stanmer safe at night?

At night, Hollingdean and Stanmer is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Brighton and Hove. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Hollingdean and Stanmer a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Hollingdean and Stanmer's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Brighton and Hove) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
